_comment: Department of Basic Education Grade 10 Mathematics P2 (statistics, analytical geometry, trigonometry, measurement and Euclidean geometry), November 2018 national common examination.
Questions and marking-guideline answers transcribed from the rendered pages of the official PDFs
(paper2.pdf, paper2_memo.pdf); the text layer does not hold usable equations. Notation:
^ for powers, sqrt() for roots, a/b for fractions, decimal commas as printed. memo_answer is the
guideline's final answer and memo_working its working (tick marks and mark descriptors left out).
The guideline is bilingual (English/Afrikaans); only the English is transcribed. Graphs and diagrams are described
in brackets in the question text. The information sheet printed with the paper is not transcribed.
The question paper and the marking guideline are scans with no text layer.
FORMAT: 100 marks, 2 hours, eight compulsory questions (Q1 14, Q2 17, Q3 11, Q4 15, Q5 12, Q6 7, Q7 9,
Q8 15). Candidates answer in a 12-page SPECIAL ANSWER BOOK (paper2_answer_book.pdf) with the frequency
table for 1.1 and the grid for 5.1.1.

questions.context: 7.2 ACS is a triangle. P is a point on AS and R is a point on AC such that PSRQ is a parallelogram. PQ intersects AC at B such that B is the midpoint of AR. QC is joined. Also, CR = PS, Ĉ1 = 50° and BP = 60 mm. [Angles: Q̂1 = CQ̂R; Ĉ1 = QĈR; R̂3 = QR̂B; B̂1, B̂2, B̂3 at B; P̂1, P̂2 at P.]
questions.memo_working: CR = PS [given]; PS = QR [opp sides of ∥m =]; CR = QR; Q̂1 = Ĉ1 = 50° [∠s opp = sides]; R̂3 = 100° [ext ∠ of Δ]; Â = R̂3 = 100° [alt ∠s, QR ∥ AS]
AP = PS [line from midpoint ∥ to one side of Δ]; RS = 120 [midpoint theorem]; QP = RS = 120 [opp sides of ∥m =]. OR ΔQBR ≡ ΔPBA (∠∠S), QB = BP = 60

questions.context: QUESTION 8 | 8.1 ABCD is a parallelogram. E and F are points on AB and DC respectively such that AE = CF. DE is produced to J and CJ is drawn. BF is produced to K and AK is drawn. [CJ meets AB at G and AK meets DC at H; Ê1 = JÊB, Ê3 = AÊD, F̂1 = KF̂D, F̂3 = BF̂C and D̂1 = EDF.] Prove that:
questions.memo_answer: AB = DC and AE + EB = DF + FC [opp sides of ∥m =]; AE = CF [given]; EB = DF; DF ∥ EB [opp sides of ∥m ∥]; EDFB is a parallelogram [one pair opp sides = and ∥]; ED ∥ FB, so DJ ∥ BK. (Alternatives use ΔAED ≡ ΔCFB [S∠S].)
Ê1 = D̂1 [corresp ∠s, AB ∥ DC]; F̂1 = D̂1 [alt ∠s, DE ∥ FB]; therefore Ê1 = F̂1. (Alternatives: via Ê3 = F̂1 and vert. opp. ∠s, or opp ∠s of parallelogram EDFB.)

questions.context: 8.2 In the diagram below O is the centre of the circle. A and B lie on the circumference of the circle. AP = BP. [OP meets chord AB at T; OA, OB, PA and PB are drawn.] Prove that:
questions.memo_answer: AP = BP [given]; OA = OB [radii]; OAPB is a kite [two pairs adj sides =]; AT = TB [one diagonal of a kite bisects the other]. OR ΔOAP ≡ ΔOBP (SSS), then ΔOAT ≡ ΔOBT (S∠S)
OT̂A = 90° [properties of a kite: diagonals ⊥]. OR OT̂A = OT̂B (ΔOTA ≡ ΔOTB) and OT̂A + OT̂B = 180° [∠s on a str. line]
